content.text: This does not look like a Windows issue, but rather a backwards compatibility issue with using different versions of Infinispan configuration/schema:
The modeshape upgrade branch bumps infinispan from 6.0 to 7.2. I suspect if you clear your fcrepo4-data directory, this error will go away.
I'm not sure if  fcrepo4-data is supposed to contain XML configuration to parse. It seems to be complaining about javax.xml.stream.XMLStreamException.
When I say "fcrepo4-data", I mean the top-level directory under which all persisted information exists... including what Modeshape uses internally.
, any news on this ticket? Are you going to be able to give it a deeper look? If not, maybe it should be closed as "Won't Fix".
I just run one-click console jar (fcrepo-webapp-4.5.1-RC-2-jetty-console.jar) on  Microsoft Windows Server 2012 R2 Base.
There is no error message. The server is up and running
, can you also verify that this issue can no longer be reproduced?
I'll give it a shot, but first:
Did you do a "mvn clean install" to build the jar or did you download it?
I just download the jar.  Didn't the
said mvn clean install on windows passed?
A successful build does not necessarily mean that the generated artifact will run okay. I don't know if there's an integration test that runs the console jar (or something along that lines).
Also, 4.5.1-SNAPSHOT build passing is not related to the behavior observed on 4.3.0.
, there is no integration test that specifically runs the "one-click" webapp. The is a manual test, however, that is now included in release testing.
It would be useful to see if you are able to build the one-click locally and start it on Windows without error. If so, I would suggest we close this ticket.
I'm checking it out and hoping it has gone away. Just to be clear, it was a Windows Server (enterprise version) not Windows (commodity) issue.
The error is still reproducible on 4.3.0 (the version against which the bug was reported), but has gone away in the latest 4.5.1 snapshot.
However, there are IT failures when doing a "mvn clean install" now on Win Server 2012 R2 with 4.5.1 shanpshot. The log is here
Perhaps there should be a row entry for it in the wiki release testing page or template for Win Server.
As for the release candidate testing, please move the conversation to the wiki:

comments.body:
This does not look like a Windows issue, but rather a backwards compatibility issue with using different versions of Infinispan configuration/schema:
Error --> '

{urn:infinispan:config:7.2}

cache-container'

The modeshape upgrade branch bumps infinispan from 6.0 to 7.2. I suspect if you clear your fcrepo4-data directory, this error will go away.
I'm not sure if fcrepo4-data is supposed to contain XML configuration to parse. It seems to be complaining about javax.xml.stream.XMLStreamException.
When I say "fcrepo4-data", I mean the top-level directory under which all persisted information exists... including what Modeshape uses internally.
Osman Din, any news on this ticket? Are you going to be able to give it a deeper look? If not, maybe it should be closed as "Won't Fix".

I just run one-click console jar (fcrepo-webapp-4.5.1-RC-2-jetty-console.jar) on Microsoft Windows Server 2012 R2 Base.

There is no error message. The server is up and running
Osman Din, can you also verify that this issue can no longer be reproduced?

Andrew Woods I'll give it a shot, but first:

Yinlin Chen Did you do a "mvn clean install" to build the jar or did you download it?

Andrew Woods Osman Din

I just download the jar. Didn't the https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Release+Testing+-+4.5.1 said mvn clean install on windows passed?

Yinlin Chen A successful build does not necessarily mean that the generated artifact will run okay. I don't know if there's an integration test that runs the console jar (or something along that lines).

Also, 4.5.1-SNAPSHOT build passing is not related to the behavior observed on 4.3.0.

Osman Din, there is no integration test that specifically runs the "one-click" webapp. The is a manual test, however, that is now included in release testing.
It would be useful to see if you are able to build the one-click locally and start it on Windows without error. If so, I would suggest we close this ticket.
Andrew Woods I'm checking it out and hoping it has gone away. Just to be clear, it was a Windows Server (enterprise version) not Windows (commodity) issue.

The error is still reproducible on 4.3.0 (the version against which the bug was reported), but has gone away in the latest 4.5.1 snapshot.

However, there are IT failures when doing a "mvn clean install" now on Win Server 2012 R2 with 4.5.1 shanpshot. The log is here https://gist.github.com/anonymous/697f9a38344695d0625a9a18cceee14b.

Perhaps there should be a row entry for it in the wiki release testing page or template for Win Server.

Thanks, Osman Din. Please close this ticket as "Fixed".

As for the release candidate testing, please move the conversation to the wiki:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Release+Testing+-+4.5.1
